correctness.rationale: Finite-difference Newton interpolation at x=0 yields D(k)|k+1. Combined with Guo et al. local prime support, only one exact prime-power component can contribute; for n=pm and p>m it has exponent one and D(n-1)=p. Repeated prime powers contribute O_s(X^(s+1-delta_s)log X), with delta_s=min(s,1)/2; the bounded unit rows are negligible for fixed s>0. Weighted PNT followed by summation over m yields zeta(s+1) and -zeta_prime(s+1), with uniform truncation and O_s(X^(s+1)/log^3 X) remainder. Independently computed direct binomial GCD for k=2..31 and checked exact prime-power valuation formula; finite checks do not justify the asymptotic.
residual_risks: Bounded independent calculations cannot replace the analytic universal argument; see proof boundary.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Even an exact all-k formula does not directly state the asymptotic distribution of its moments; standard prime summation plus a convergent multiplier weight is required. No dominating moment theorem identified.

originality.rationale: Guo et al full lawful open text gives the zero-versus-positive prime criterion (and its exact local support), not moments. The 2026-10-12 published exact prime-power valuation theorem computes D(k) for every k but does not provide weighted mean or logarithmic correction, nor an asymptotic theorem dominating it. Summing over primes and extracting the zeta derivative is an additional analytic distribution result, not identical to pointwise computation.
residual_risks: An earlier generic prime-times-small-factor summatory theorem could imply the moment constants without being indexed as a binomial-GCD result.
No uniformity as s down to zero; numerical first-moment finite ratios are not proofs of asymptotic behavior.

value.rationale: The first two moments of a natural OEIS binomial-row GCD statistic, especially the zeta-derivative secondary constant across all fixed real positive exponents, quantify nontrivial mass carried by rare large-prime rows; this is a motivated distribution result beyond reproducing a known table.
residual_risks: Value assessment concerns the natural mathematical question, not publication priority or downstream theorem size.

final_claim: For D(k)=gcd_{2<=q<=k+1} binom(qk,k), each fixed s>0 has the two-term positive-real moment law X^(s+1)/((s+1)log X){zeta(s+1)+[zeta(s+1)/(s+1)-zeta_prime(s+1)]/log X+O_s(log^-2 X)}.
limitations: Fixed s>0 only; lower-order error not uniform near s=0; Guo local prime criterion is a cited prior input.
